title: Power Lessons From China
gist: Teaser: Gavekal's AJ Cortese warns the US data center boom faces a power crunch that could become systemic by 2028, that captive hyperscaler plants are an expensive stopgap limited by turbine and transformer shortages, and that China is ahead on flexible batteries and distributed renewables.

insights.claim: Delays and cancellations of US data centers due to electricity shortages have so far been sporadic but could become systemic by some point in 2028 and force a significant slowdown in construction.
insights.so_what: The AI buildout has a hard power constraint around 2028 that may cap capex growth.
insights.speaker: AJ Cortese

insights.claim: Hyperscalers' main response, building captive power plants, is an expensive stopgap that will itself be slowed by shortages of turbines and transformers.
insights.so_what: Turbine and transformer suppliers hold pricing power while captive power adds cost to AI capex.
insights.speaker: AJ Cortese

insights.claim: Building more on-grid capacity will take time, so the US needs to use batteries and distributed renewables to make power demand and supply more flexible, an effort in which China is already ahead.
insights.so_what: Flexibility assets such as storage are the near-term solution; China's lead is a competitive edge.
insights.speaker: AJ Cortese
